name: Cybersecurity
tagline: Protect people, companies and systems from attacks — and respond when they happen.

overview.summary: Cybersecurity professionals defend networks, applications, cloud systems and data from attackers. Some work on defence (monitoring alerts in a Security Operations Centre, responding to incidents), some on offence (ethical hacking and penetration testing to find weaknesses first), and some on governance (risk, compliance and security policy). With AI helping attackers write phishing emails and malware faster, organisations need more skilled defenders — and people who can secure AI systems themselves.
whyTrending: BLS projects information security analyst jobs to grow 21% from 2025 to 2035, with a 2025 US median wage of $129,180.
ISC2's 2025 Cybersecurity Workforce Study found 95% of respondents report at least one skills gap on their team, and AI and cloud security are the most needed skills.
Ransomware, data breaches and AI-powered phishing keep rising, and new regulations require companies to report and manage cyber risk.
In Bangladesh, banks, MFS providers and government digital services are investing in security operations after high-profile incidents and growing digital payments.

trendSources.label: Reveal IT Talent Survey 2026 — cybersecurity engineers among hardest roles to fill (38%)

roles.title: SOC Analyst
roles.description: Monitors security alerts, investigates suspicious activity and escalates real incidents — the most common entry-level security job.

roles.title: Penetration Tester / Ethical Hacker
roles.description: Legally attacks systems and applications to find vulnerabilities and writes reports with fixes.

roles.title: Cloud Security Engineer
roles.description: Secures AWS/Azure/GCP environments: identity, network controls, misconfiguration detection and compliance.

roles.title: Incident Responder / DFIR Analyst
roles.description: Handles breaches end to end: containment, forensic analysis, recovery and lessons learned.

roles.title: Application Security (AppSec) Engineer
roles.description: Works with developers on secure code review, threat modelling and security testing in CI/CD pipelines.

roles.title: GRC Analyst
roles.description: Manages governance, risk and compliance — policies, audits, ISO 27001, PCI DSS and vendor risk.

beginner: Networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, ports, subnets
Security concepts: CIA triad, authentication, encryption, hashing
Common attacks: phishing, malware, brute force, SQL injection, XSS
intermediate: SIEM tools (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Elastic) and log analysis
Web application testing with Burp Suite and the OWASP Top 10
Cloud security basics: IAM, security groups, logging
advanced: Securing AI/LLM applications (prompt injection, data leakage)

stack.note: Entry-level listings frequently mention CompTIA Security+, ISC2 CC or vendor SIEM experience; senior roles mention CISSP, OSCP or cloud security certifications.

roadmap.title: Foundations
goals: Learn networking basics (OSI model, TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP)
Get comfortable with the Linux command line
Start the free ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC) course
Capture and read traffic in Wireshark
roadmap.milestone: Comfortable explaining how a web request travels across a network and where attacks happen.

roadmap.title: Defence and attack basics
goals: Set up a home lab with virtual machines
Practise web vulnerabilities with PortSwigger Web Security Academy
Ingest logs into a free SIEM (Splunk Free or Elastic) and write detections
Complete the TryHackMe SOC Level 1 path or Blue Team Labs challenges
roadmap.milestone: A documented home lab with at least three detection rules and screenshots.

roadmap.title: Specialise and certify
goals: Choose a track: SOC/blue team, pentesting or cloud security
Take the ISC2 CC exam or prepare for CompTIA Security+
Write 3 detailed write-ups of labs or CTF challenges
Join a CTF competition (picoCTF, local university CTFs)
Apply for SOC analyst internships or junior roles
roadmap.milestone: A certification (or exam booked), CTF write-ups on a blog and an updated CV.

projects.title: Home security lab
projects.description: Set up Kali Linux and a vulnerable VM (e.g. Metasploitable) in VirtualBox and document a safe, isolated testing environment.

projects.title: Phishing email analyser
projects.description: A Python script that parses email headers and links, flags suspicious signs and produces a short report.

projects.title: SIEM detection lab
projects.description: Send Windows and Linux logs to Splunk or Elastic, simulate attacks with Atomic Red Team and write detections mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.

projects.title: Web app penetration test report
projects.description: Test OWASP Juice Shop, find and exploit vulnerabilities, and write a professional report with risk ratings and fixes.

projects.title: Cloud security posture scanner
projects.description: Build a tool that scans an AWS account (your own free-tier lab) for misconfigurations — public buckets, open security groups, weak IAM — and suggests fixes.

interview.question: What is the CIA triad?
interview.answer: Confidentiality (only authorised access), Integrity (data is accurate and unaltered) and Availability (systems work when needed) — the core goals of security.

interview.question: Difference between encryption and hashing?
interview.answer: Encryption is reversible with a key and protects confidentiality. Hashing is one-way, producing a fixed-length digest used to verify integrity or store passwords (with salt).

interview.question: What is SQL injection and how do you prevent it?
interview.answer: Inserting malicious SQL into input fields to manipulate a database. Prevent it with parameterised queries, input validation, least-privilege DB accounts and an ORM.

interview.question: What happens when you type a URL into a browser?
interview.answer: DNS resolves the domain to an IP, the browser opens a TCP connection, performs a TLS handshake for HTTPS, sends an HTTP request and renders the response.

interview.question: What is a false positive in a SOC?
interview.answer: An alert that flags benign activity as malicious. Too many waste analyst time, so detections are tuned to balance false positives and missed attacks.

interview.question: Describe the incident response lifecycle.
interview.answer: Preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident lessons learned (NIST).

interview.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
interview.answer: Users and systems get only the minimum access needed to do their job, limiting damage if an account is compromised.

interview.question: Symmetric vs asymmetric encryption?
interview.answer: Symmetric uses one shared key (fast, e.g. AES). Asymmetric uses a public/private key pair (e.g. RSA, ECC) for key exchange and signatures; TLS uses both.

interview.question: What is MITRE ATT&CK used for?
interview.answer: A knowledge base of real attacker tactics and techniques, used to map detections, find coverage gaps and describe attacks consistently.

interview.question: How would you secure a web login page?
interview.answer: HTTPS, strong password hashing (bcrypt/Argon2), rate limiting and lockout, MFA, secure session cookies, CSRF protection and logging of failed attempts.

demandNotes.bangladesh: High and rising in banks, MFS, telecom and government digital services. SOC analyst and security-operations roles are the main entry points.
demandNotes.remote: Good for pentesters, bug-bounty hunters and managed-security service staff. Fully remote SOC roles often require time-zone overlap.
demandNotes.global: Very high. 21% projected growth in the US and widespread skills gaps reported by ISC2.
